name: December 20, 2022 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  DECEMBER 20, 2022
  VARIOUS TELECONFERENCE LOCATIONS
  5:30P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Jenner called the meeting to order at 5:34 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Vice Chair Cayley Jenner; and Commissioners Georgia Goldfarb, Suzanne
  Guldimann, and Alicia Peak

  ABSENT: Chair Dane Skophammer

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Acting Community Services Director; Kate Gallo,
  Recreation Manager; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Guldimann led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Chair
  Skophammer absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on December 16, 2022.

ITEM I  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  4-0; Chair Skophammer absent

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the November 15, 2022
  Parks and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  during November 2022.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Poetry Stones for John Struloeff and Ann Buxie
  Recommended Action: Review and approve the installation of two poetry stones
  honoring former Poet Laureate John Struloeff and current Poet Laureate Ann
  Buxie.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the Malibu Arts Commission provides a Poet Laureate appointment
  recommendation and City Council approves the Poet Laureate appointment. She
  stated the first Poet Laureate was appointed in 2018 and the term is two years.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated the Poet Laureates and the Poet Laureate
  Committee have worked hard to expand literary arts. She stated the Committee
  organized poetry workshops and arts and education programs.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated poetry stones are installed at the end of the Poet Laureate' s term.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Acting Community Services Director
  Riesgo stated poetry stones ranged from $1,500 to $2,500 and it included the stone,
  engraving, delivery, and installation.

  Commissioner Goldfarb was in favor of placing two stones at Legacy Park for John
  Struloeff and Ann Buxie.

  In response to Vice Chair Jenner, Commissioner Guldimann stated a contest was
  held at Juan Cabrillo Elementary School and the selected poet received a poetry
  stone.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Acting Community Services Director
  Riesgo stated the Commission would review the placement of future poetry stones.

  Commissioner Goldfarb expressed her concern about the accumulation of poetry
  stones over time.

  Commissioner Peak stated the installation of one stone would occur every two
  years. She stated the stones could be placed in several places at Legacy Park.

  In response to Vice Chair Jenner, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the poetry stones weighed over eight hundred pounds.

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Vice Chair Jenner seconded a motion to
  approve the installation of two poetry stones honoring former Poet Laureate John
  Struloeff and current Poet Laureate Ann Buxie. The question was called, and the
  motion canied 4-0; Chair Skophammer absent.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the poem and Poet Laureate name were engraved on the stone.

  Commissioner Peak suggested including the year on the poetry stone.

  Commissioner Guldimann requested adding an online Poet Laureate biography
  with a quick response (QR) code.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated she would provide the
  suggestions to the Malibu Arts Commission.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Manager Gallo provided an update on the Michael Landon Center
  flooring project and December holiday events.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on the Charmlee
  Wilderness Park trailhead signs and the commission meeting schedule.

CONSENSUS By Consensus, the Commission agreed to conduct a Park Tour of Legacy Park, the
  Ioki property, and Malibu Bluffs Park starting at 4:00 p.m. on January 17, 2023,
  cancel the February 21, 2023 Regular meeting, and hold a Special meeting on
  February 23, 2023 at 5:30 p.m.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Guldimann thanked staff for the installation of the Charmlee
  Wilderness Park trailhead signs.

  Commissioner Peak stated the gate on Grayfox Street at Malibu Elementary School
  was open on the weekend.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Park Security
  Malibu Bluffs Park Turf Improvements

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 6:09 p.m., Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded
  a motion to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried
  4-0; Chair Skophammer absent.
